stem: A health system shifts from fee-for-service toward value-based payment. Which statement best describes the intended change?

options.A: Payment is increasingly tied to the number of billable services delivered while quality and patient outcomes play a smaller role in financial incentives.
options.B: Payment increasingly rewards quality of care and performance rather than service volume alone, aligning incentives with better care.
options.C: Payment removes formal quality measurement from reimbursement decisions, allowing organizations to focus primarily on increasing procedural volume.
options.D: Payment separates reimbursement from patient outcomes and care quality because value-based models are designed only to simplify billing administration.

rationale: CMS states that value-based programs reward providers with incentive payments for the quality of care they provide and are intended to move payment toward quality rather than quantity of services. B directly reflects that shift. A describes the volume emphasis value-based programs are intended to move away from, while C and D incorrectly remove quality and performance from payment decisions.
educational_objective: Distinguish value-based payment from fee-for-service by recognizing that value-based programs link financial incentives to quality and performance rather than service volume alone.
source_locator: What are the value-based programs?; Why are value-based programs important?; original value-based programs section linking quality performance to payment.
source_claim_supported: Value-based programs reward providers with incentive payments for quality and move payment toward quality rather than quantity of care; quality performance is linked to payment.

source_original.stem: A health system shifts from fee-for-service toward value-based payment. Which statement best describes the intended change?

options.A: Payment is increasingly tied to the number of billable services delivered, while quality and patient outcomes play a smaller role in financial incentives.
options.B: Payment increasingly rewards the quality and outcomes of care rather than service volume alone, aligning financial incentives with better patient care.
options.C: Payment removes formal quality measurement from reimbursement decisions, allowing organizations to focus primarily on increasing procedural volume.
options.D: Payment separates reimbursement from patient outcomes and care quality, because value-based models are designed only to simplify billing administration.

source_original.rationale: CMS describes value-based programs as rewarding quality rather than service quantity alone. Option B captures that shift toward quality and outcomes. Option A describes the volume emphasis of fee-for-service rather than the intended value-based direction. Option C incorrectly removes quality measurement from reimbursement. Option D incorrectly separates payment from quality and outcomes.
source_original.source_detail: CMS — Value-Based Programs: value-based programs reward health care providers with incentive payments for quality of care and move payment toward quality rather than quantity/service volume alone. CMS Value-Based Programs page modified 2026-03-10; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, continuity, confidentiality, quality/cost-effective care, legal/ethical rights and assignment/delegation activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key and construct but narrowed 'quality and outcomes' to CMS's exact broad language of quality/performance rather than implying every value-based program directly pays on patient outcome measures.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Final answer states quality/performance vs volume only; it avoids overgeneralizing specific outcome-measure structures across every program.

distractor_audit.D: Value-based models are not merely billing simplification and do link payment to quality.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B reflects CMS policy intent.
audit_findings.cueing: Parallel payment-policy statements; no second answer.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Verified 2026 CMS page and softened overbroad outcome wording.
